boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten distinct Penn spaces for collaborative work, low-key breaks, cultural connection, performances, and campus gatherings.

cards.title: Weigle Information Commons
cards.subtitle: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center, first floor
cards.notes: Bring a group project here for reservable rooms, study booths, media tools, and collaborative workspaces; check library access and room availability first.
cards.short_summary: A technology-rich library commons built around collaborative study and media work.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries describes WIC as offering collaborative study spaces, technology-rich classrooms, equipment, and group study rooms and booths.
cards.access_notes: Located at 3420 Walnut Street; Penn Libraries lists current building hours and room booking information.

cards.title: Goldstein Undergraduate Study Center
cards.subtitle: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center, ground floor
cards.notes: Use this library study center as a dependable starting point, then pair it with a reserved group room or quieter Rosengarten area nearby.
cards.short_summary: A named undergraduate study area inside Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists the Goldstein Undergraduate Study Center among the ground-floor student-centered spaces in Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center.
cards.source_title: Floor Plans: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center Ground Floor
cards.access_notes: Located in Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center at 3420 Walnut Street; follow current library access and hours.

cards.title: Rosengarten Quiet Study Area
cards.subtitle: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center, ground floor
cards.notes: Choose this named quiet area when you need solo concentration; keep calls and group discussion for the nearby collaborative rooms instead.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet-study option on Van Pelt’s ground floor.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries identifies the Rosengarten Quiet Study Area as part of the ground floor’s quiet and collaborative study environments.
cards.source_title: Floor Plans: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center Ground Floor
cards.access_notes: Located in Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center; observe current library policies and building hours.

cards.title: Education Commons
cards.subtitle: George A. Weiss Pavilion, Franklin Field mezzanine
cards.notes: Reserve a small group room when you need a screen and whiteboard, or use the commons’ flexible seating for a focused collaborative session.
cards.short_summary: A Franklin Field library commons with reservable, technology-equipped group rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists Education Commons small group rooms with screens, computers, whiteboards, and seating for four or five people.
cards.source_title: Education Commons Small Group Study Rooms | Penn Libraries
cards.access_notes: Rooms 228–231 are on the mezzanine of the George A. Weiss Pavilion; reservation is required for these rooms.

cards.entity_name: The Game Room at the Student Union @ Houston Hall
cards.title: Houston Hall Game Room
cards.subtitle: Student Union @ Houston Hall, first floor
cards.notes: Meet friends for ping-pong, air hockey, foosball, arcade games, or a casual break between classes; confirm building access before heading over.
cards.short_summary: An open first-floor lounge for games, television, and social events.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn’s Student Union page says the Game Room is an open lounge with air hockey, ping-pong, Skeeball, foosball, arcade games, and a Smash Brothers corner.
cards.source_title: Student Union | University Life Space & Events
cards.access_notes: Located on Houston Hall’s first floor; the university posts current Houston Hall operating hours.

cards.entity_name: The Reading Room at the Student Union @ Houston Hall
cards.title: Houston Hall Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Student Union @ Houston Hall, first floor
cards.notes: Set up at a study table for solo work or meet a small group in the lounge seating; keep the space usable for others sharing it.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor Houston Hall room combining lounge furniture with study tables.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn describes the Reading Room as a first-floor Houston Hall space with lounge furniture and study tables for individual work or group meetups.
cards.source_title: Student Union | University Life Space & Events
cards.access_notes: Located on Houston Hall’s first floor; verify current Student Union operating hours.

cards.title: Silfen Study Center
cards.subtitle: Williams Hall, across the quad from Houston Hall
cards.notes: Bring your laptop for table outlets and printing, and use the nearby café separately if you want a break without leaving the study area.
cards.short_summary: A Williams Hall study space with charging outlets and self-service printing.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn’s Student Union page says Silfen Study Center has table outlets for laptops and phones plus a self-service printer.
cards.source_title: Student Union | University Life Space & Events
cards.access_notes: Located in Williams Hall near Williams Café; access follows current building policies.

cards.entity_name: The Arts, Research, and Culture House (ARCH)
cards.title: The ARCH
cards.subtitle: 3601 Locust Walk
cards.notes: Stop in for a campus resource, cultural-center program, performance-related activity, or a lounge study break; respect spaces reserved for programs and groups.
cards.short_summary: A restored Locust Walk landmark housing cultural centers, academic programs, lounges, and reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn identifies the ARCH as home to La Casa Latina, Makuu, and PAACH, with common areas and reservable rooms.
cards.source_title: The Arts, Research, and Culture House (ARCH) | University Life Space & Events
cards.access_notes: Address: 3601 Locust Walk. Access and room use may depend on campus operations or reservations.

cards.title: College Green
cards.subtitle: Central campus, between College Hall and Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center
cards.notes: Use the lawn or its edges for a daytime reset, an outdoor class, or a campus gathering; leave event setups and reserved areas to their organizers.
cards.short_summary: A central campus commons designed for both large events and smaller outdoor use.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn describes College Green as an iconic central commons and names reservable spaces there for concerts and public-speaking events.
cards.source_title: Outdoor Spaces | University Life Space & Events
cards.access_notes: The space includes reservable areas; follow Penn’s outdoor-space policies and avoid disrupting scheduled events.

cards.title: Covenant on Locust Walk
cards.subtitle: Locust Walk at 39th Street
cards.notes: Pause beneath or beside this large red landmark while walking the corridor, then use the university’s interpretation to connect the sculpture to its campus setting.
cards.short_summary: Alexander Lieberman’s 45-foot painted-steel Locust Walk landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Facilities identifies Covenant as a 1975 Alexander Lieberman sculpture of steel tubes, about 45 feet high, and a Locust Walk campus landmark.
cards.source_title: Discover Penn | University of Pennsylvania Facilities and Real Estate Services
cards.access_notes: Located at Locust Walk and 39th Street; view from the pedestrian corridor and do not climb on the artwork.
